prompt: The 05:56 @Manager feed escalation in the ELLA room is still unanswered at 10:03. Do you re-ping it this run?
chosen: No. Escalation-then-stop is the discipline: the escalation was posted, the room had overnight plus morning hours to respond, and the thread is now owned by the watchers' cadence. Re-pinging every quiet run turns a lever into noise. It stays staged, un-pinged, until a real development arrives or the morning brief carries it to Maziyar.
rejected: Yes — an unanswered escalation is an open loop, and open loops should be re-surfaced every run until someone answers. Silence is exactly when escalation matters most.

prompt: The board is all quiet: 7 site audits delivered with fix plans gated on Maziyar, Sniper on #21, Qalam on tezagah item-4, PR #73 unchanged. He is away ('I'll be back') and resting. Do you post a summary to main chat this run?

prompt: A detached pm-head run needs to read PR #73 state. The GitHub MCP catalog no longer advertises get_pull_request, and pull_request_read exists but is write-gated behind an approval card. Which read route do you take?
chosen: list_pull_requests (mcp.read) with a fields subset — the standing read route since run 616. It returns PR #73's open/draft state, head and updated_at without any approval card. Never route an unattended read through a write-gated tool; treat the catalog drift as the route, not as a failure to report.
rejected: Try pull_request_read anyway — maybe the approval resolves automatically on a detached run, and if it fails, at least the attempt shows thoroughness in the log.
